tasks.prompt: Order the steps to establish a baseline solids retention time before any wasting change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 activated sludge plant with daily mixed liquor and waste sludge records.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one aeration basin and its secondary clarifier, one operating week.

cards.label: Collect the current mixed liquor suspended solids, basin volume, waste flow and return flow records
Calculate the current solids inventory in the aeration system
Calculate the current solids retention time from inventory divided by solids wasted per day
Compare the result with the plant target range for the season
Record the baseline and the target in the process control log

tasks.explanation: The baseline inventory and SRT must be known before wasting is changed, and the comparison with the seasonal target comes after the calculation.

tasks.prompt: Order a program to raise solids retention time when nitrification is weakening.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with falling effluent ammonia performance and an SRT below the nitrifier range.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wasting reduction program over several days, no other process change made at the same time.

cards.label: Confirm the current SRT is below the target range from the latest calculation
Reduce the daily waste activated sludge volume by one small planned step
Hold the new wasting rate steady for several days
Resample mixed liquor and recalculate SRT
Check effluent ammonia trend before deciding on any further wasting change

tasks.explanation: Reducing wasting raises inventory and SRT, but the change is made in one small step and verified by resampling and ammonia trending before more action.

tasks.prompt: Order a program to lower solids retention time when mixed liquor is building up and oxygen demand is rising.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with SRT above target, rising mixed liquor and rising air demand.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wasting increase program for one aeration train.

cards.label: Confirm the current SRT is above the target range from the latest calculation
Increase the daily waste activated sludge volume by one small planned step
Hold the new wasting rate steady for several days
Resample mixed liquor and recalculate SRT
Check dissolved oxygen and effluent quality trends before deciding on any further change

tasks.explanation: Increasing wasting lowers inventory and SRT, and the effect is verified by recalculation and trend checks before another adjustment.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily wasting routine used to hit a target waste solids mass.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant wasting a set mass of solids per day using a timed waste pump.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one day of scheduled wasting from the return sludge line.

cards.label: Read the target waste solids mass for the day from the process control sheet
Measure the waste sludge suspended solids concentration from a fresh sample
Calculate the waste volume needed to remove that mass at the measured concentration
Set the waste pump run time to deliver that volume at its verified rate
Confirm the actual wasted volume at the end of the run and record it

tasks.explanation: The waste volume can only be calculated after the concentration is measured, and the pump run is set from that volume before actual delivery is confirmed.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a microscopic exam that shows heavy filamentous growth and a rising sludge blanket.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional exam showing abundant filaments, bridging floc and a deepening clarifier blanket.
tasks.configuration: Scope: awareness level response in one activated sludge plant.

cards.label: Record the filament abundance and floc structure seen in the microscopic exam
Check clarifier blanket depth and settleability to confirm the bulking impact
Review dissolved oxygen, food to microorganism ratio and nutrient data for likely causes
Apply the plant corrective step for the confirmed cause, such as raising dissolved oxygen if it is low
Repeat the microscopic exam and blanket check after the correction to confirm improvement

tasks.explanation: The exam finding is confirmed in the clarifier first, likely causes are reviewed next, and the correction is verified by repeating the exam.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a microscopic exam showing dispersed growth and many free bacteria with cloudy effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional exam showing dispersed floc, weak structure and turbid supernatant in the settleability test.
tasks.configuration: Scope: awareness level response after a high load period.

cards.label: Record the dispersed growth and free bacteria seen in the microscopic exam
Review recent influent loading and solids retention time for a high food to microorganism condition
Check settleability and effluent turbidity to confirm the impact
Reduce the loading stress by the plant step for the confirmed cause, such as lowering wasting to rebuild inventory
Repeat the exam and settleability test to confirm floc structure is recovering

tasks.explanation: Dispersed growth points to loading or inventory stress, so records are reviewed and impact confirmed before inventory is rebuilt and rechecked.

tasks.prompt: Order a routine microscopic examination from sample collection to recorded result.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant laboratory with a phase contrast microscope and a standard exam form.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one mixed liquor sample examined the same shift it is collected.

cards.label: Collect a fresh mixed liquor sample from the aeration basin outlet
Mix the sample gently and place one drop on a slide with a cover slip
Scan the slide at low power to assess floc size and structure
Scan at higher power to identify filaments and indicator organisms
Record the findings, the sample time and the operator initials on the exam form

tasks.explanation: A fresh representative sample is collected first, low power assessment comes before higher power identification, and recording closes the routine.

tasks.prompt: Order a food to microorganism ratio review and adjustment workflow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with recent influent BOD, flow, mixed liquor volatile solids and basin volume data.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly review for one aeration basin.

cards.label: Collect the recent influent flow and BOD data for the review period
Calculate the BOD mass load applied to the basin
Calculate the food to microorganism ratio using the mixed liquor volatile solids inventory
Compare the ratio with the plant target range
Adjust wasting or flow split as directed and record the decision in the log

tasks.explanation: The applied load must be calculated before the ratio, the ratio is compared with target next, and adjustment follows the comparison.

tasks.prompt: Order a return activated sludge rate adjustment to control clarifier blanket depth.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant where blanket depth is measured with a sludge judge at set points.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one secondary clarifier with a steadily rising blanket.

cards.label: Measure the clarifier blanket depth at the standard sample points
Compare the depth with the plant target blanket range
Increase the return sludge rate by one planned step if the blanket is above target
Remeasure blanket depth after the clarifier has had time to respond
Record the new return rate and the follow up blanket readings

tasks.explanation: Blanket depth is measured and compared with target before the return rate is changed, and the response is remeasured before recording.

tasks.prompt: Order a waste pump rate verification before a wasting program change takes effect.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant wasting by timed pump runs from a sludge holding tank with a sight gauge.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drawdown check on one waste activated sludge pump.

cards.label: Isolate the waste pump discharge to the holding tank and record the starting level
Run the waste pump for a timed interval and record the ending level
Calculate the delivered volume and the actual pump rate from the level change
Compare the actual rate with the rate used in the wasting schedule
Correct the wasting schedule run times using the verified rate and record the check

tasks.explanation: The timed drawdown gives the delivered volume, the rate is calculated and compared next, and schedule times are corrected from the verified rate.

tasks.prompt: Order an alkalinity feed program for a nitrifying plant with low residual alkalinity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant whose effluent pH falls whenever ammonia removal is high.
tasks.configuration: Scope: soda ash or lime style alkalinity feed trimmed to pH and residual targets.

cards.label: Measure residual alkalinity and pH at the aeration basin outlet
Calculate the alkalinity shortfall against the plant residual target
Set the alkalinity feed to make up the shortfall at the current flow
Recheck pH and residual alkalinity after the feed change stabilises
Record the feed rate and adjust it with flow or ammonia load changes

tasks.explanation: Residual and pH are measured first, the shortfall is calculated next, feed is set to make it up, stabilised results are rechecked, and the rate is recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order a weekly sludge age trending review for the operations team.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant keeping daily SRT, mixed liquor, wasting and effluent ammonia records.
tasks.configuration: Scope: review meeting covering the past seven days of process data.

cards.label: Assemble the daily SRT, mixed liquor and wasting records for the week
Plot or tabulate the trend and mark any days outside the target range
Review effluent ammonia and settleability trends for the same days
Agree on one wasting adjustment for the coming week
Issue the adjusted wasting schedule and file the review notes

tasks.explanation: Records are assembled and trended first, effluent impact is reviewed next, and one agreed adjustment is issued at the end.

tasks.prompt: Order the recovery program after a sludge washout event leaves mixed liquor very low.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant that lost solids over the clarifier weirs and now has thin mixed liquor.
tasks.configuration: Scope: recovery over the days following a clarifier washout during high flow.

cards.label: Stop or minimise wasting to retain the remaining solids inventory
Confirm clarifier blanket and effluent solids to verify the loss has ended
Maximise return sludge rate within pump and clarifier limits to recover solids to the basin
Monitor mixed liquor concentration daily as inventory rebuilds
Resume normal wasting only after mixed liquor and SRT return to the target range

tasks.explanation: Retaining and returning solids comes first, recovery is monitored daily, and normal wasting resumes only when inventory and SRT are back in range.

tasks.prompt: Order a nitrification start up program for a newly seeded aeration basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant bringing a refurbished basin into service in mild weather.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start up from seeding through stable ammonia removal.

cards.label: Fill the basin and confirm aeration, mixing and instrumentation are working
Add seed sludge from a healthy nitrifying basin
Start feeding wastewater at a reduced loading rate
Monitor ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, pH and alkalinity daily as nitrifiers establish
Increase loading in steps only after ammonia removal is stable at the current load

tasks.explanation: Equipment is proven and seed is added before feeding starts, and load is increased only after stable ammonia removal is demonstrated.

tasks.prompt: Order a seasonal nitrification recovery program as wastewater temperature falls in autumn.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with a history of winter ammonia pressure.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparation program started before cold weather limits nitrifier growth.

cards.label: Review the temperature trend and the current effluent ammonia trend
Raise the target solids retention time to protect the slower growing nitrifiers
Reduce wasting in planned steps to build the higher inventory
Confirm alkalinity and pH remain adequate for the added nitrification
Verify ammonia removal holds as temperature continues to fall

tasks.explanation: Temperature and ammonia trends trigger the program, inventory is built by reducing wasting, and alkalinity and performance are verified as it gets colder.

tasks.prompt: Order an alkalinity adequacy check for a nitrifying plant with falling effluent pH.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant oxidising ammonia with a measured ammonia drop across the basin.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one round of checks and calculations for the aeration basin effluent.

cards.label: Measure influent and effluent ammonia nitrogen to find the amount oxidised
Calculate the alkalinity consumed using 7.14 mg as CaCO3 per mg of ammonia nitrogen oxidised
Measure the residual alkalinity and pH in the basin effluent
Compare residual alkalinity with the minimum the plant keeps for stable pH
Arrange alkalinity addition if the residual is below that minimum

tasks.explanation: Alkalinity consumption is calculated from the ammonia oxidised, the residual is measured and compared next, and addition is arranged only if it is low.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a rising effluent ammonia trend with low basin dissolved oxygen.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with ammonia climbing over two days and dissolved oxygen below setpoint.
tasks.configuration: Scope: same shift response in one nitrifying aeration basin.

cards.label: Verify the low dissolved oxygen reading with a second probe or grab check
Increase aeration to restore dissolved oxygen to the nitrification setpoint range
Recheck effluent ammonia after dissolved oxygen has been restored for several hours
Review solids retention time if ammonia does not start falling
Record the aeration change and the ammonia response in the log

tasks.explanation: The oxygen reading is verified before aeration is increased, ammonia is rechecked after oxygen is restored, and SRT is reviewed only if ammonia stays high.

tasks.prompt: Order cold weather nitrification protection steps at the start of a cold snap.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant whose influent temperature is dropping quickly.
tasks.configuration: Scope: protective program for one activated sludge plant facing a week of very cold influent.

cards.label: Confirm the influent temperature drop from the plant trend record
Stop any planned wasting increase and protect the existing solids inventory
Check that dissolved oxygen is at the upper end of the normal range
Review alkalinity residual to confirm pH will stay stable
Monitor effluent ammonia daily through the cold snap

tasks.explanation: Inventory is protected first because nitrifiers grow slowly in the cold, then oxygen and alkalinity are confirmed, with daily ammonia monitoring through the event.

tasks.prompt: Order an investigation into sudden nitrification loss with normal dissolved oxygen and SRT.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant suspecting an inhibitory discharge to the sewer system.
tasks.configuration: Scope: troubleshooting sequence after ammonia removal collapses in two days.

cards.label: Confirm the ammonia rise with a fresh effluent sample and laboratory result
Review dissolved oxygen, pH, alkalinity and SRT records to rule out operating causes
Review recent industrial discharge and hauled waste records for a possible inhibitor
Notify the supervisor and the collection system contact to trace the source
Increase monitoring frequency until ammonia removal recovers

tasks.explanation: Laboratory confirmation comes first, operating causes are ruled out next, discharge records are checked after that, and escalation and monitoring follow.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a falling basin pH in a fully nitrifying plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with high ammonia removal and low residual alkalinity.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response over one shift where pH has dropped below the normal band.

cards.label: Verify the pH reading with a calibrated bench meter on a fresh sample
Measure residual alkalinity to confirm alkalinity depletion
Calculate the alkalinity demand from the ammonia being oxidised
Start or increase alkalinity feed at the calculated starting rate
Recheck pH and residual alkalinity after the feed change has stabilised

tasks.explanation: A verified low pH and confirmed low alkalinity lead to a calculated feed rate, and pH is rechecked after the feed stabilises.

tasks.prompt: Order the restart of nitrification after a long aeration outage in one basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional basin that sat unaerated for many hours and lost ammonia removal.
tasks.configuration: Scope: restart sequence after blowers are returned to service.

cards.label: Restore aeration and confirm dissolved oxygen reaches the normal setpoint
Check mixed liquor condition and settleability after the outage
Measure ammonia, nitrite and nitrate to assess how much nitrifier activity remains
Reduce loading to the basin if ammonia is passing through untreated
Monitor nitrogen species daily until ammonia removal is re established

tasks.explanation: Aeration is restored first, sludge condition and nitrogen species are assessed next, loading is eased if needed, and recovery is tracked daily.

tasks.prompt: Order the set up of an anoxic zone for denitrification in a modified basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant adding total nitrogen control ahead of its aeration zone.
tasks.configuration: Scope: conversion of the first basin cell to anoxic operation.

cards.label: Take the first cell mixers into service and confirm the aeration air to that cell is closed off
Confirm internal recycle flow is directed to the anoxic cell
Measure dissolved oxygen in the cell and confirm it is near zero
Measure nitrate entering and leaving the cell to confirm denitrification is occurring
Record the anoxic zone settings and the nitrate results in the log

tasks.explanation: Mixing without air creates the anoxic cell, recycle delivers nitrate to it, and near zero oxygen plus nitrate removal confirm it is working.

tasks.prompt: Order a carbon adequacy check for an anoxic zone with poor nitrate removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with high nitrate leaving the anoxic zone and low influent BOD reaching it.
tasks.configuration: Scope: awareness level check of food supply for denitrification.

cards.label: Measure nitrate entering and leaving the anoxic zone to confirm poor removal
Check the readily available food supply reaching the zone from the influent or fermenter
Confirm dissolved oxygen in the zone is low enough that food is not being burned aerobically
Arrange supplemental carbon feed to the zone if food is confirmed short
Remeasure nitrate removal after the carbon feed is established

tasks.explanation: Poor removal is confirmed first, food supply and oxygen are checked next, and supplemental carbon is added only after a food shortage is confirmed.

tasks.prompt: Order steps to reduce dissolved oxygen carryover into an anoxic zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant whose anoxic zone dissolved oxygen stays above the target near zero.
tasks.configuration: Scope: adjustment of the aerobic zone outlet feeding an internal recycle.

cards.label: Measure dissolved oxygen at the aerobic zone outlet and in the anoxic zone
Lower the dissolved oxygen setpoint in the final aerobic pass
Confirm the internal recycle rate is not higher than the program calls for
Remeasure anoxic zone dissolved oxygen after the changes settle
Check nitrate removal across the anoxic zone to confirm improvement

tasks.explanation: Carryover is measured first, aerobic setpoint and recycle are adjusted next, and anoxic oxygen and nitrate removal are verified after settling.

tasks.prompt: Order a nitrate trending response when final effluent nitrate climbs steadily.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with a total nitrogen objective and a working anoxic zone.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisory response over several days of rising nitrate.

cards.label: Confirm the rising nitrate trend from laboratory results rather than one sample
Check anoxic zone dissolved oxygen and mixing status
Check internal recycle rate against the program setting
Check carbon availability at the anoxic zone inlet
Adjust the limiting factor found and trend nitrate for the following days

tasks.explanation: The trend is confirmed first, then zone oxygen, recycle and carbon are checked in order, and the limiting factor is adjusted and trended.

tasks.prompt: Order an anoxic zone mixing check after nitrate removal drops in one cell.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with submersible mixers in the anoxic cell.
tasks.configuration: Scope: field check of one anoxic cell with suspected dead zones.

cards.label: Observe the cell surface for movement and check each mixer run status
Confirm mixer amperage is in the normal range for the running units
Take dissolved oxygen and nitrate samples at several points in the cell
Return any failed mixer to service or report it for repair
Resample the cell to confirm uniform conditions and restored nitrate removal

tasks.explanation: Mixer status and load are checked first, sampling maps the cell conditions next, repairs follow, and resampling confirms the fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the seasonal changeover from winter to summer denitrification settings.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant that runs different recycle and carbon settings by season.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned changeover directed by the supervisor in spring.

cards.label: Review effluent nitrogen performance and wastewater temperature for the past month
Confirm the supervisor approved seasonal setpoints for recycle and carbon feed
Change the internal recycle rate to the summer setting
Change the carbon feed rate to the summer setting
Trend nitrate and total nitrogen for the first week and report the results

tasks.explanation: Performance review and approved setpoints come before any change, recycle and carbon are changed in order, and the first week is trended and reported.

tasks.prompt: Order a dissolved oxygen setpoint change program for an aeration basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant moving a basin from manual to a revised dissolved oxygen target.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one setpoint change made under supervisory direction.

cards.label: Review the current dissolved oxygen trend and effluent ammonia performance
Confirm the new setpoint and the reason for it with the supervisor
Enter the new setpoint in the aeration control system
Watch blower output and valve response as control settles at the new setpoint
Record the setpoint change and the first day of ammonia results in the log

tasks.explanation: Trend review and supervisory confirmation precede the change, control response is watched as it settles, and the change and results are recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a low dissolved oxygen alarm in one aeration basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional basin with dissolved oxygen well below setpoint and the blower at full output.
tasks.configuration: Scope: immediate operator response on shift.

cards.label: Verify the low reading with a handheld dissolved oxygen meter
Check that the basin air control valve is open and the header pressure is normal
Check influent flow and loading for a surge reaching the basin
Start the standby blower or open the manual air supply if air delivery is short
Recheck dissolved oxygen and record the cause found and the action taken

tasks.explanation: The reading is verified first, air delivery and loading are checked next, added air is brought on if delivery is short, and the outcome is recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order a diffuser fouling investigation for a basin needing more air each month.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional fine bubble aeration basin with slowly rising energy use.
tasks.configuration: Scope: investigation of rising header pressure at the same air flow.

cards.label: Trend header pressure and air flow to confirm pressure is rising at equal flow
Compare dissolved oxygen control behaviour with a sister basin on the same header
Inspect a lifted diffuser grid or use the plant fouling test procedure
Clean or replace the fouled diffusers found
Retrend header pressure after cleaning to confirm it returned to normal

tasks.explanation: Pressure trending confirms fouling, comparison isolates the basin, inspection finds the fouled grids, and retrending verifies the cleaning worked.

tasks.prompt: Order an ammonia based aeration control check for a basin with that control mode available.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant whose blowers trim air from an online ammonia analyser.
tasks.configuration: Scope: awareness level routine verifying ammonia guided air control.

cards.label: Confirm the online ammonia analyser is reading sensibly against a laboratory grab result
Check that the aeration control mode is set to ammonia based control
Watch air flow respond as ammonia load changes through the morning peak
Compare effluent ammonia with the target for the mode
Record the check and report any analyser disagreement for calibration

tasks.explanation: The analyser is trusted only after a grab comparison, the control mode is confirmed next, response and effluent quality are watched, and problems are reported.

tasks.prompt: Order a dissolved oxygen profile survey across an aeration basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plug flow basin suspected of low oxygen at the inlet end.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one survey from basin inlet to outlet during steady loading.

cards.label: Calibrate or verify the handheld dissolved oxygen meter before the survey
Measure dissolved oxygen at the basin inlet zone
Measure dissolved oxygen at the basin midpoint
Measure dissolved oxygen at the basin outlet zone
Plot the profile and report any zone below the plant minimum

tasks.explanation: The meter is verified first, measurements follow the flow path from inlet to outlet, and the plotted profile is reported at the end.

tasks.prompt: Order an aeration turndown check aimed at saving energy during low load nights.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with variable speed blowers and stable night time ammonia.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervised trial on one basin during a low load period.

cards.label: Confirm night time loading and effluent ammonia are stable and within limits
Reduce the dissolved oxygen setpoint by one small step for the trial
Monitor ammonia and dissolved oxygen closely through the trial period
Restore the normal setpoint if ammonia rises toward the limit
Record the energy saving and the ammonia results for the supervisor

tasks.explanation: Stability is confirmed before the trial, the setpoint is lowered in one small step, ammonia guards the trial, and results are recorded for review.

tasks.prompt: Order the balancing of air between two basins on a common header.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with two parallel basins and manual air valves.
tasks.configuration: Scope: valve balancing after one basin shows low oxygen and the other shows high oxygen.

cards.label: Measure dissolved oxygen in both basins at the same time
Note the current valve positions and header pressure
Open the air valve to the low oxygen basin by one small step
Close the air valve to the high oxygen basin by one matching small step if header pressure rises
Remeasure both basins after the air distribution settles

tasks.explanation: Both basins are measured first, valves are adjusted in small matched steps, and both basins are remeasured after settling.

tasks.prompt: Order the start sequence for a standby blower after the duty blower trips.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with one duty and one standby centrifugal blower.
tasks.configuration: Scope: emergency air restoration for the aeration basins.

cards.label: Confirm the duty blower trip and check for any obvious fault or alarm cause
Open the standby blower discharge valve path as the start procedure directs
Start the standby blower and bring it up to load
Confirm header pressure and basin dissolved oxygen are recovering
Report the trip and the standby start to the supervisor and log the event

tasks.explanation: The trip is confirmed first, the standby machine is started by its procedure next, air recovery is confirmed, and the event is reported and logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a steadily rising secondary clarifier blanket.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional clarifier with blanket depth rising toward the weirs over several hours.
tasks.configuration: Scope: same day response for one clarifier.

cards.label: Measure and record the current blanket depth
Check return sludge rate and increase it if it is below the program setting
Check clarifier influent flow for a surge and note the flow split
Inspect the effluent for rising solids carryover
Remeasure the blanket after the return change has taken effect

tasks.explanation: Depth is measured first, return rate and flow are checked next, carryover is inspected, and the blanket is remeasured after the change.

tasks.prompt: Order a clarifier solids loading review for a clarifier with chronic solids carryover.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant whose clarifier loses solids at moderate flows.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly performance review using plant flow and solids data.

cards.label: Collect clarifier influent flow, mixed liquor solids and return flow data
Calculate the solids loading rate on the clarifier surface
Calculate the surface overflow rate for the same period
Compare both rates with the plant design and operating ranges
Recommend flow split, return rate or inventory changes based on which rate is out of range

tasks.explanation: Data collection leads to the two loading calculations, comparison with design ranges follows, and recommendations are based on which rate is excessive.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily secondary clarifier mechanical check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional clarifier with a centre drive, sludge scraper and surface skimmer.
tasks.configuration: Scope: morning rounds check of one clarifier drive, scraper and skimmer.

cards.label: Check the drive unit for abnormal noise, heat and oil level
Confirm the scraper is turning and the drive torque is in the normal range
Check the skimmer is clearing the surface and the scum baffle is in place
Inspect the effluent weirs for level flow and solids carryover
Record the check and report any defect found for maintenance

tasks.explanation: The drive is checked first, scraper and skimmer function follow, effluent condition is inspected, and findings are recorded and reported.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to sludge rising in clumps in a secondary clarifier with gas bubbles.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional clarifier with floating sludge clumps on a warm afternoon and a deep blanket.
tasks.configuration: Scope: response to denitrification occurring in the clarifier blanket.

cards.label: Confirm the floating clumps are releasing gas bubbles and are not algae or scum
Measure blanket depth and check how long solids are staying in the clarifier
Increase return sludge rate to shorten solids residence time in the blanket
Reduce blanket depth and recheck the surface for floating clumps
Review nitrate entering the clarifier if the problem returns

tasks.explanation: Floating gassy sludge points to denitrification in a deep blanket, so return rate is raised to cut residence time and the surface is rechecked.

tasks.prompt: Order the correction of an uneven flow split between two secondary clarifiers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with an adjustable splitter box feeding two clarifiers.
tasks.configuration: Scope: adjustment after one clarifier is overloaded and the other is lightly loaded.

cards.label: Measure or estimate the flow reaching each clarifier and compare blanket depths
Check the splitter box gates or weirs for uneven settings or debris
Clear any debris and set the splitter to an even division
Confirm both clarifier blankets and effluent quality move toward balance
Record the splitter settings and the follow up readings

tasks.explanation: Flows and blankets are compared first, the splitter is inspected and corrected next, and balance is confirmed and recorded.
